register: Polite; the plain counterpart is だろう.

examples.reading: あしたはあめでしょう。
これはたかいでしょう。

usage: Your own confident guess: 明日は雨でしょう, 'it will probably rain'. Think of a weather forecaster.
With rising intonation it asks for agreement: 'right?'. 高いでしょう? is 'expensive, isn't it?'.
It ends the clause, so nothing more attaches except particles like ね, よ, or けど.

compare.difference: かもしれない is weaker: it only says something is possible. でしょう expects it to be true.
らしい reports what you heard or saw. でしょう is your own conclusion.
